grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, flour, oats, almonds, sugar, cinnamon and sunflower oil are all plain cupboard staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Peaches, raspberries in June, oats, almonds and sunflower oil are everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a bowl, a fork and scales, and the technique is simple mixing and scattering.

works.reason: Around 700g of fruit under a 240g oat and flour topping bound with 5 tbsp oil, baked at 180°C fan for 30 to 35 minutes, gives a sound crumble for four, though the juices may stay a little loose with only 1 tsp cornflour.

honest_times.reason: Stoning four peaches, chopping almonds and rubbing together the topping fits in 15 minutes, and 55 minutes total covers baking and resting.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used in the steps under its true name, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Midsummer raspberries are the clear star of a fruit crumble, which suits a June afternoon.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, friendly British English with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is mostly fruit with oats and almonds and modest added sugar, a crumble a family would happily make again.
